\[
(x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 = r^2,
\qquad
H(a, b, r) = \frac{\#\{\text{edge pixels on the circle } (a, b, r)\}}{\#\{\text{points on the circle}\}}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(a, b\): The center of a circle
- \(r\): The radius
- \(H\): The share of the circle that is edge

A circle has a center (a, b) and a radius r. For each radius, an edge pixel lies on all circles whose center is r away from it. These centers form a circle themselves. Every edge pixel draws this circle of votes into the accumulator of its radius. Where many of these circles cross, many edge pixels lie on one circle, so peaks are circles. Here scikit-image divides each count by the number of points on the circle. So H is the share of the circle that is edge, and circles of different sizes compare fairly. Duda and Hart described this extension of the Hough transform to curves.
